description: We are Astroforge, a multidisciplinary team of Systems and Electronic Engineering students from Bolivia. We combine software development, hardware integration, and data analysis to build innovative tech solutions.
summary: We developed AstroHealth, an integrated software that collects, analyzes, and visualizes astronaut vital signs in real time. Addressing in-space health challenges, our platform tracks biometric data and provides early anomaly alerts to support crew self-management. This is essential for deep-space missions, where communication delays require autonomous medical monitoring to ensure astronaut well-being and mission success.
details:
AstraHealth is a low-cost, real-time life-support monitor for crews in closed environments. An ESP32 reads a MAX30102 (heart rate and SpO2), a DS18B20 (temperature) and an MQ-135 (air quality, estimated CO2-equivalent ppm) every second and sends the data by MQTT to a live web dashboard. Each sensor is rated Nominal, Caution or Critical. When readings stay critical, a "critical moment" is saved in a MySQL database and Google Gemini AI suggests immediate actions and preventive recommendations.

Based on NASA's "Hostile/Closed Environments" and "Distance from Earth" hazards and the Risk of Hypoxia, it combines sensors to give early warnings (bad air + high heart rate + falling SpO2) and helps crews act on their own when help is far away. On Earth, it can protect people in mines, shelters and any closed workplace.
